method: Preliminary verse-by-verse screening, primary Hebrew passage and contemporary translation at specified locators consulted; no critical manuscript collation, no public verification, no assertion of dependence. Reconcile with main and prior open branches before integration.

verses.finding: Divorce, reconciliation and prohibition of harmful retention; Deuteronomy 24:1–4 addresses divorce documentation and subsequent remarriage, but does not match the Quranic prohibition of retention to cause harm.
Prohibition on preventing divorced women from remarrying after agreed lawful terms; no exact earlier rule established.
Nursing for two full years, parental support and consensual weaning; Exodus 21:10–11 concerns maintenance rights in a different household/legal context, not breastfeeding duration.
Four-month-and-ten-day waiting period for widows; Deuteronomy 25:5–10 addresses childless widow and levirate duty without this waiting interval.
Permitted indirect marriage proposals during waiting period, with restrictions on secret arrangements; no exact earlier passage established.
Divorce before consummation or specification of dowry, with appropriate provision; no exact earlier source established.
Half the specified dowry in divorce before consummation, subject to remission; no exact earlier legal counterpart established.
Guarding prayers, especially middle prayer; no precise pre-Islamic source assigned.
Prayer during fear, walking or riding; no source-specific parallel assigned.
Provision and residence for widows for a year, with textual/legal relationship to 2:234 requiring internal Quranic exegesis; no exact earlier counterpart assigned.

candidates.shared: Both regulate dissolution of marriage and subsequent marital status.
candidates.difference: Deuteronomy specifies divorce documentation and forbids a first husband reclaiming a woman after intervening marriage; Quran 2:231 emphasizes fair retention/release and prohibits harmful retention.

candidates.shared: Both prescribe material obligations within family or marital relations.
candidates.difference: Exodus concerns obligations to a woman in a specific servitude/marriage context, not nursing, parental division of costs, or a two-year period.

candidates.shared: Both regulate a widow's marital status after the death of her husband.
candidates.difference: Deuteronomy prescribes levirate marriage arrangements for a childless widow and a refusal ceremony; Quran specifies a four-month-ten-day waiting period without a levirate command.

questions: Distinguish 2:234 waiting period and 2:240 widow provision in classical interpretation before mapping external texts.
Consult textual-critical Hebrew and Greek witnesses for Deuteronomy 24–25 and Exodus 21; record composition and manuscript dates separately.
Investigate Mishnah Yevamot and Ketubot with dating and version specificity, without treating later redaction as direct Quranic source.
Reconcile open coverage PRs and private queue; verify RLS before publication.
